title: 3-Year Treasury Note auction (January new issue) — the block's largest leg, and the natural experiment that separates the SOMA add-on from cycle position
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), the four FlateDecode content streams inflated PER PAGE and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates independently of both proposals. The page-3 row reads verbatim `3-Year NOTE / Thursday, January 07, 2027 / Monday, January 11, 2027 / Friday, January 15, 2027`, carrying NO `R` and no `T` against the page legend `R --denotes reopening` / `T --denotes TIPS` — a NEW ISSUE, matching `reopening: "No"` on all 212 3-Year rows fiscaldata `auctions_query` returns back to 2009-01-07. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-07 coupon announcement. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICALISED 2026-09-09 from TWO proposals — `proposals/treasury-3y-note-2027-01-11.from-treasury-10y-note-2027-01-12.json` and `...from-treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13.json` — both read in full first per EVENT-RESEARCH.md, and both left in place (the canonical file shadows them). Their date, new-issue read, Monday slot and Friday 2027-01-15 settlement all reproduce against a fresh page-by-page fetch of the same primary. FOUR AMENDMENTS, all measured this session. (1) THE ALWAYS-NEW-ISSUE CLAIM IS BIGGER THAN EITHER PROPOSAL STATED, and it is what makes this leg a controlled experiment. One proposal cites 'zero of the 45 3-Year auctions since 2023-01-01'; `auctions_query` returns 212 rows back to 2009-01-07 and `reopening` reads `No` on 212 of 212. So across 18 years cycle position is a CONSTANT for this security — yet the SOMA add-on since 2018 ranges $0.00B to $32.39B with 27 outright zeros in 104 prints. A variable that never moves cannot explain an outcome that moves that much: the December 10-Year sibling's 'NEW issue 35/35 positive, mean $12.35B' is not a fact about newness. (2) THE CONFOUND IS NAMED AND MEASURED. 10-Year new issues occur only in Feb/May/Aug/Nov — exactly the refunding-month settlements. Splitting this security's 104 post-2018 prints the same way: Feb/May/Aug/Nov settlements run 34/34 positive at a $16.35B mean, every other month 43/70 at $2.61B, with cycle position identical in all 104. (3) THE SIBLING'S POOL QUERY KEY IS WRONG ON A ROLLED SETTLEMENT, and this is load-bearing. The 10-Year ledger reads NY Fed SOMA for holdings maturing on the SETTLEMENT date; the correct key is the security's MATURITY date (the 15th), which Treasury settles on the next business day when it falls on a weekend. Settlement-date keying returns $0.00B for 2026-08-17 where the true `soma_holdings` is $31.62B — a 100% error. Maturity-date keying validates on five out-of-sample settlements (2026-04-15 -0.17%, 2026-05-15 0.00%, 2026-08-17 -0.01%, 2026-02-17 -0.00%, 2025-11-17 +0.02%), three of them rolled. 2027-01-15 is a Friday, so January is unaffected — the METHOD every future pulse in this family runs is what changes. (4) THE SPLIT LAW HOLDS ON 32 SETTLEMENTS, NOT 3. Add-on share vs offering share across every non-zero 3/10/30 coupon block since 2023-01-01: maximum absolute deviation 0.0002 percentage points, across six different offering grids and roll ratios from 5.0% to 100.0%. WHAT THIS LEG IS: the largest of the three at $58B against the 10-Year's $39B and the 30-Year's $22B, so it takes 48.74% of whatever SOMA rolls at the 2027-01-15 settlement. NY Fed holdings as of 2026-09-02 show exactly two TIPS maturing 2027-01-15 — 912810PS1 ($5.61B par + $3.68B inflation compensation) and 912828V49 ($12.24B + $4.68B), $26.21B together, coupons only with no bill on that date — so the expected add-on is ~$12.9B on a ~$70.9B total accepted, the largest single non-competitive award in the block and the one most likely to be misread as demand. It cannot be: bid-to-cover is computed net of the add-on on BOTH sides (matched to +/-0.005 on 10 of 10 recent prints, where total/total reads 2.278 against a published 2.650), and corr(add-on, bid-to-cover) = -0.143 across the 30-auction $58B run — a null measured on the security that takes the market's largest add-ons, up to 29% of its own offering. SIZE IS INFERRED, NOT PUBLISHED: $58B would be the 34th consecutive since 2024-04-09 (30 completed through 2026-09-08, with 10-06, 11-09 and 12-07 in between); it is decided at the 2026-11-04 refunding and published on 2027-01-07. STRUCTURE: opens a compressed Mon/Tue/Wed block (3-Year 01-11, 10-Year 01-12, 30-Year 01-13) all settling Friday 2027-01-15, bracketed by the PDF's own `Holiday - Friday, January 01, 2027 - New Year's Day` and `Holiday - Monday, January 18, 2027 - Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.`; the session also carries 13-week and 26-week bills, which settle Thursday 01-14, one day BEFORE the coupon block — so unlike 2026-01-15 the two blocks are cleanly separated on the calendar. Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
